diagnosis: HBV calibrated with DDS (NSE objective; 3000 runs, then 2500 more starting from that result) on daily flow from 1971-10 to 1997-12, after a one-year warm-up. Initial stores were set close to their long-term equilibrium levels. Calibration NSE is 0.858, KGE 0.872, r 0.93, and the model overestimates total flow by about 5% (PBIAS +5%). The parameters are physically plausible: FC about 219 mm, LP 0.72, BETA 2.0, K1 0.22, K2 0.034 (a moderate groundwater baseflow, consistent with the fractured and intergranular aquifers), PERC about 2 mm/d and MAXBAS about 2 d. Snow matters little here (2.5% of precipitation falls as snow). The SFCF of 0.72 and the CWH pinned at zero are weakly identified and have little effect on the result. Weaknesses: the model overestimates flow overall, which could come from the three reservoirs (abstraction and regulation) or from errors in the PET inputs. Reservoir-regulated low flows and the timing of some peaks are likely captured poorly. The biggest flood peaks are probably underestimated (simulated maximum about 16 mm/d against 21 observed). The two DDS runs ended at very similar parameter values, so I am fairly confident in the parameter set. I did not run a split-sample test, so how well it transfers to an independent period is untested. I expect the 1998–2008 NSE to be about 0.80–0.85.
